title: From call for proposals to a published program
disclosure: Human verification, including Turnstile, is disabled for this automated hackathon demo and can be re-enabled for a production event.

voice.notes: Lead with organizer value. Let important UI state remain visible for at least two seconds after each action. Do not narrate routine navigation.

scenes.title: One connected event workflow
visuals: Open on the public schedule at desktop width
Pan through a populated schedule, then the public speaker gallery
End on the Session Party wordmark
scenes.narration: The hackathon thesis is simple: kill the event-operations SaaS stack without losing the workflow. Session Party replaces the disconnected form builder, review tool, speaker portal, scheduling system, live desk, and widget vendor with one open-source Cloudflare application. We will follow one event record through the product while the overlays expose the primitives underneath.

scenes.title: The organizer's operational home
visuals: Use the visible demo-role control to continue as Organizer
Open AI Engineer Sandbox
Show the event overview and left navigation
Briefly pause on readiness counts
scenes.narration: The organizer surface is a React Router application over registered, typed operations. Effect services enforce authorization and domain errors; D1 stores event-scoped records. The result replaces a collection of admin SaaS dashboards with one operational graph where proposals, speakers, tasks, content, agenda, communications, and publication share identity and audit history.

scenes.title: Structured proposal intake
visuals: Open Forms and the primary CFP
Show fields, semantic roles, tracks or formats, routing, and publication state
Open the public CFP in an anonymous context
Demonstrate a conditional question changing with an earlier answer
Pause on the submit action without exposing personal information
scenes.narration: This replaces form SaaS with a typed domain model. Semantic field roles identify canonical title, abstract, track, and speaker data; conditional rules drive the public form; Effect Schema validates the operation boundary. Submissions land in D1 and abuse budgets remain durable. Human verification is disabled only for this automated hackathon replay and can be restored for a production event.

scenes.title: Committee review with human control
visuals: Switch through the visible demo-role control to Reviewer
Open an assigned proposal in the review workbench
Show rubric scores, rationale, committee comments, and the optional AI suggestion
Save a human score or show an already saved review
Return as Organizer and show the acceptance decision
scenes.narration: This replaces review SaaS with role-scoped projections and versioned evidence. The reviewer receives only assigned proposals; blind rounds redact identity; rubric scores, rationale, and comments remain separate records. An AI suggestion is optional and non-authoritative. The human override and final organizer decision are explicit, persisted, and auditable rather than disappearing into a spreadsheet cell.

scenes.title: A reusable speaker portal
visuals: Continue as the synthetic Speaker account
Show the accepted Taming 40-Minute CI session
Open tasks and due dates
Show the reusable profile and event-specific biography and social links
Show the uploaded headshot preview after reload
Show task-linked files, logistics, and readiness
scenes.narration: This replaces speaker-management SaaS with a projection over the accepted session, task workflow, reusable profile, and reviewed event snapshot. D1 keeps the workflow metadata; R2 stores versioned uploads. The headshot and slides remain attached to the same speaker and session identity, while organizer comments, due dates, logistics, and readiness update without another integration or nightly sync.

scenes.title: Acceptance becomes a schedulable talk
visuals: Return as Organizer and open the accepted-proposal backlog
Create the talk for Taming 40-Minute CI without retyping it
Show Priya and the Platform & Infra track carried over
Show multi-day room and time placement
Pause on named room and speaker conflict validation
Show zero blocking conflicts and publication readiness
scenes.narration: This replaces scheduling SaaS with explicit agenda operations and optimistic versions. Accepted proposal fields become a talk without re-entry. A normalized speaker-identity graph catches collisions even when the demo contains multiple event-scoped speaker rows. Room and speaker conflicts are named, while the draft remains editable. With zero blocking conflicts, the agenda is ready to publish.

scenes.title: PartyServer Durable Object live control
visuals: Open the agenda live-show control
Select a scheduled session and move it to ready
Start the session, hold it, and resume it
Reload the organizer page while the session is running
Reopen live-show control and prove the running state survived reconnection
Reset the synthetic demo state
scenes.narration: This is the most interactive replacement. The React live desk connects through PartySocket to an EventRoom PartyServer Durable Object—one authoritative state machine per event for the current session, running timer, holds, and targeted cues. We transition from ready to running, hold, and resume. After a full reload and websocket reconnection, the same running state survives because it lives in the Durable Object, not one browser. The recorder resets the synthetic state afterward.

scenes.title: Publish once, serve every audience
visuals: Show the publication revision and publish or refresh action
Open the anonymous schedule
Show mobile width, search, filters, and a session detail
Open the matching public speaker record
scenes.narration: This replaces the publishing and widget SaaS layer. An agenda publish operation creates an immutable, privacy-filtered audience revision. Stable embeds resolve the current live revision, while HTML, JSON, XML, and iCalendar expose portable outputs with CORS and ETags. The event owns both the source data and the distribution contract.

scenes.title: A portable, open-source result
visuals: Show the embed builder and stable widget URL
Flash the JSON, XML, and iCalendar outputs
End on the public program and repository mark
scenes.narration: The same open projection powers the attendee pages, speaker gallery, personal schedule, stable embeds, and standards-based feeds. Session Party kills the SaaS dependency by replacing it with inspectable operations, owned data, realtime Durable Object state, and portable public outputs.

scenes.title: One source of truth
scenes.narration: Session Party takes an event from call for proposals to a live public program in one open-source workspace.

scenes.title: Collect and decide
scenes.narration: Structured CFP fields and conditional routing produce clean proposal data. Assigned reviewers score against a rubric, discuss evidence, and remain in control of clearly labeled AI suggestions. Hackathon demo verification is disabled for automated replay and can be re-enabled for production.

scenes.title: Onboard speakers
scenes.narration: After acceptance, the speaker sees the session, tasks, logistics, profile, and uploads in one portal. The saved headshot persists after reload and appears on the organizer's matching record.

scenes.title: Build and run the program
scenes.narration: The accepted proposal becomes a schedulable talk without retyping. A PartyServer Durable Object coordinates the live session state, timer, holds, and reconnects in real time.

scenes.title: Publish everywhere
scenes.narration: One immutable release powers the mobile schedule, speaker gallery, stable embeds, feeds, and calendar exports. That is the whole event workflow—connected, auditable, and portable.
